answers.answer:
No. SCOPe 2.08 gives no basis for calling them homologous, even though they share a full sccs. In SCOPe 2.08, d1s9za_ (PDB 1s9z chain A; protein 'Amyloidogenic design-1', sunid 103785; species Synthetic, sunid 103786) and d1hqja_ (PDB 1hqj chain A; protein 'Unnamed design-1', sunid 100906; species Synthetic, sunid 64668) are both classified as k.40.1.1. The lineage is: class k 'Designed proteins' (sunid 58788) > fold k.40 'Designed trimeric coiled-coil' (100903) > superfamily k.40.1 (100904) > family k.40.1.1 'Designed trimeric coiled-coil' (100905). They differ only at the protein (dm) level.

Class k is not a true evolutionary class. It holds synthetic peptides and proteins that were designed artificially, and SCOPe groups them for convenience by shape (here, a designed trimeric coiled coil). In classes a–g, sharing a family means clear common descent and sharing a superfamily means probable common descent. Neither applies in class k. The k.40.1.1 'family' and k.40.1 'superfamily' simply reflect the shared designed coiled-coil shape. SCOPe makes no claim that either peptide descends from the other or from a common natural ancestor.

The resemblance has other explanations. Both are short synthetic heptad-repeat peptides, and similar coiled coils arise readily from low-complexity repeats and from designs that converge on the same target. Designers may also have borrowed from the same natural template, such as the GCN4 leucine zipper. That is shared engineering lineage, not biological homology.

Do not transfer anything between them. That covers function, oligomeric state, stability, and amyloid or fibril-forming behaviour, which is the defining property of the 1s9z 'amyloidogenic' design. Do not use either as a template for the other on the strength of the shared sccs. Do not treat either as a representative of a natural coiled-coil family, such as the a.2 or h.1 groups with natural homologues. Note too that 'Unnamed design-1' is just a placeholder name, not a functional annotation.

Any claim of real relatedness would need outside evidence beyond SCOPe: the primary design papers showing that one sequence was derived from the other or that both came from the same parent. Even then, that would be design ancestry, not evolutionary homology. A significant sequence alignment would also not count, because heptad repeats are low-complexity and inflate similarity scores.

In summary, they share the same fold, superfamily and family labels in 2.08, but because they sit in class k those labels show structural or design similarity only, not homology.
